source_text.body:
Build a tax document gathering and bookkeeping workflow
A poster used Claude Code to build a tax document gathering hub, generate bookkeeping reports, and then a full bookkeeping app.
·
Mar 1, 2026
Done with
CC
Claude Code
CL
Claude
What they did
The thread describes three related Claude Code setups. The original poster planned a local-folder tax workflow with redacted files, model-training opt-out, and a curated IRS knowledge base that would only answer when it could cite a source; in comments, one person said they built a tax document hub that ingests forms, flags likely deductions and missing documents, and prepares either TurboTax-ready inputs or one organized PDF, while another used Claude skills to generate repeatable bookkeeping reports and then turned that into a bookkeeping app.
How it went
The reported result was working prep and reporting tools rather than autonomous tax filing: one user said it helped gather documents and organize outputs, and another said the reporting workflow grew into a full app. No performance numbers were given, and both tax-related comments stressed caution around legal or accuracy risks.
Worth knowing
The main catch was privacy and risk: they opted out of training, redacted personal data, and one builder chose not to release the tool because of legal implications.
Try it yourself
with
Claude Code
Copy prompt
Help me build a tax document gathering workflow for [tax year] in the folder [path]. Create a checklist of the documents I need (such as W-2s, 1099s, receipts, and bank statements) based on my situation: [filing status, income types, deductions]. Then scan the files in the folder, mark which items are present or missing, and produce a simple bookkeeping summary by category. Don't move, rename, or delete any files without showing me the plan first.
Original source: https://www.reddit.com/r/buildinpublic/comments/1rjb60q/tax_season_experiment_building_an_ai_tax_filing
